dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Citlali, I've been told that the merchants here are all protected by the organizers. I'm afraid confronting him myself will be more trouble than it's worth.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh, do I have to do everything myself?

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Oh, please, Granny Itztli, have mercy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chasca! Citlali! What are you, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's a long story... Basically, a few members of the Flower-Feather Clan brought word from Nod-Krai that someone was selling "Wayob fragments" at this expo.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Pretty serious stuff. So, I brought Citlali here to get to the bottom of it, and hopefully keep things under control.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Okay, well as it turns out, we've been tasked with mediating any disputes like this.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Are you intending to try and stop me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please, Granny Itztli.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *sigh* Look, I'm not trying to be difficult, but you don't need me to tell you that our Wayob are not for sale! ...Wait a second...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This is just a shard of a Wayob pillar... And its power is long gone, so it no longer has any connection whatsoever to the Wayob. So, tell me. How much did they pay you to ship these out of Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Umm... about 800 thousand Mora a piece.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Apparently, people outside of Natlan don't know all that much about our culture. Some people take one look at those pillars and start bragging that they've found a Wayob fragment.

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: I didn't wanna correct them, 'cause that way I could drum up the price...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh... Forget it. Since you asked me so nicely, I'll let him stay here until the expo's over. No point making a mountain out of a molehill.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Granny Itztli!

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you, Granny Itztli!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, don't start thinking you're off the hook! Once this is over, you're going straight to Biram to face the music.

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Eek...
